DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 75 s. 2022 AUG 04 2022 ATTY. ANTHONY C. NUYDA Regional Director, DILG-Region V Rizal St., Legazpi City Dear RD Nuyda: This has reference to your Memorandum dated July 7, 2022 concerning the series of appointment of non-elected officials as Punong Barangays in Barangay Cataingan, Masbate. Hereunder are the pertinent factual antecedents as we culled from your Memorandum: 1. The incumbent Punong Barangay (PB) of Domorog, Pawican, and Madamba voluntarily tendered their irrevocable resignation on May 18, May 31 and June 2, all of this year; 2. All three (3) resignations were subsequently approved by you through a letter addressed to the concerned PBs; 3. With the resignation of these PBs and your subsequent approval thereon, a permanent vacancy was created in the said position; 4. All incumbent sangguniang barangay members, including the highest-ranking, issued a duly notarized waiver stating that they waived and relinquished their rights to succeed as Punong Barangay; 5. Thereafter, Mayor Felipe L. Cabataöa issued appointments on the following in replacement to the PBs who voluntarily resigned: • Philip Floyd K. Cabatafia IV for Barangay Domorog, Cataingan, Masbate in replacement of Wilfredo A. Booc. • Engr. Filemon A. Bailon for Barangay Pawican, Cataingan, Masbate in replacement of Maria Novie M. Sarzuelo • Dante G. Sauro for Barangay Madamba, Cataingan, Masbate in replacement of Junnifer L. Bareja. In the herein case, the voluntary resignation of herein concerned PBs and the Mayor's subsequent approval thereon precipitated permanent vacancies in the aforesaid positions. Accordingly, in filling up such vacancies, Section 44 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160, hereinafter referred to as the Code) shall apply, thus: Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

"Section 44. Permanent Vacancies xxx. (b) If a permanent vacancy occurs in the office of the punong barangay, the highest ranking sanggunian barangay member or, in case of his permanent inability, the second highest ranking sanggunian member, shall become the punong barangay. (c) A tie between or among the highest ranking sanggunian members shall be resolved by the drawing of lots. (d) The successors as defined herein shall serve only the unexpired terms of their predecessors. For purposes of this Chapter, a permanent vacancy arises when an elective local official fills a higher vacant office, refuses to assume office, fails to qualify, dies, is removed from office, voluntarily resigns, or is otherwise permanently incapacitated to discharge the functions of his office. For purposes of succession as provided in the Chapter, ranking in the sanggunian shall be determined on the basis of the proportion of votes obtained by each winning candidate to the total number of registered voters in each district in the immediately preceding local election." (Emphasis supplied) Thus, applying the above-cited provisions, the highest-ranking sangguniang barangay members shall become the Punong Barangays, and who shall serve the unexpired terms of their predecessors. At this juncture, it may be well to stress that it behooves upon the highest-ranking sangguniang barangay member to assume such vacancy in the position of Punong Barangay. The act of herein concerned sangguniang barangay members in relinquishing their rights to assume the position of Punong Barangay by virtue of a notarized waiver is misplaced. The Department has been consistent in its opinion that the first-ranking sangguniang barangay member cannot waive his/her right to assume the position of punong barangay in the event of permanent vacancy therein in favor of the second-ranking sangguniang barangay member, thus: "xxx please be informed that the same is not legally feasible. Although the Civil Code recognizes the waiver of rights, the same Code provides that such waiver of rights must not be contrary to law and public policy. Considering the constitutional dictum that a "public office is a public trust", there is equally a principle in administrative law that a public office cannot be bargained away nor could it be subject of waiver. When one seeks an elective position and has in fact been elected thereto by the mandate of the electorate who voted him into office, he should assume all the duties and responsibilities pertaining thereto, including the duty to assume a higher office and he cannot just "throw off' such responsibilities at his own pleasure, except by tendering his resignation." 1 DILG Legal Opinion No. 14, series Of 2001. Page 2 of 3

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: AN Undersecr ry for Local Government OUSLG/MLl/LLLS-LRALLD/jam/dp cc: ATTY. ANTHONY C. NUYDA Director, DILG-V Rizal St., Legazpi City Page 3 of 3
